title: Nodera service index
description: A list of trackers and rendezvous services. This is the format of the project's own list (services/official.json) AND of any third-party store a user adds in the app — deliberately one format, so a store is not a second-class citizen and the built-in list is not a special case. An index is a set of HINTS: every service in it still proves who it is with its own Ed25519 signature, and nothing here grants any authority over world state.

schema_version.description: 1. Bumped only for a breaking change; a reader that does not know the version must refuse the index rather than guess at it.

name.description: What to call this store in a list of stores.

updated.description: ISO date this index last changed. Informational — freshness that matters is measured, not declared.

kind.description: tracker = discovery. rendezvous = reachability behind NAT. A host running both publishes two entries: they are separate services on separate ports with separate identities.

endpoints.description: Routes to try, best first. More than one is normal and useful: a name plus a literal address survives a DNS outage, and an IPv4 plus an IPv6 route survives a client with only one of them.

node_id.description: The service's stable identity, 32 lowercase hex characters, if the operator has published it. Optional, and its absence is normal — a peer that has never seen this service trusts it on first use either way. When present it turns a hijacked DNS name from something a peer accepts into something a peer notices.

operator.description: Who runs it. A contact, not an authority.

region.description: Rough location, so a peer far from every listed service can see that rather than infer it from latency.
